title: nil
summary: The 'no value' value. A variable that is nil holds nothing; table keys set to nil are deleted; accessing something that doesn't exist gives nil.

details.heading: Where nil comes from
details.body: Undeclared or unassigned variables read as nil. Reading a table key that doesn't exist gives nil. Calling a function with no matching return gives nil. `FindFirstChild()` returns nil when nothing is found.

details.heading: nil deletes
details.body: Assigning `t.key = nil` removes that key from the table. This is the only way to delete a dictionary entry.

details.heading: nil is falsy
details.body: In `if` conditions, only `nil` and `false` count as false. `0`, empty strings and empty tables are all *truthy*.

explanation.whatItIs: `nil` is Luau's way of saying 'there is nothing here'. It is an actual value with its own type, used everywhere an absence needs to be represented: a search that failed, a slot that's empty, an argument that wasn't passed.
explanation.whyItExists: Programs constantly need to express 'not found' or 'not set yet'. Without nil you'd need separate sentinels like -1 or "" for every type.
whenToUse: Check for nil before using a value that might not exist: `if part then ... end` or `if part ~= nil then`
Set a table key to nil to remove it: `inventory["sword"] = nil`
Return nil from a function to signal 'no result'
whenNotToUse: Don't use nil to mean zero or empty-string in game logic — they are different values with different meanings
Don't store nil in the *array part* of a table (holes break `#t` and `ipairs`)
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local pet            --> nil (never assigned)
print(pet)           --> nil

pet = "Dragon"
print(pet)           --> Dragon

pet = nil            --> the label falls off; value forgotten
print(pet)           --> nil
```
nil is the absence of a value — the empty hook where a value could hang.
tips: `if not x then` catches both `nil` and `false` — usually what you want
Use the or-default pattern: `local speed = config.Speed or 16`
Most 'attempt to index nil' crashes are a missing nil check — see the gotcha entry
commonMistakes: Assuming `0` or `""` is falsy — only `nil` and `false` are falsy
Forgetting that `FindFirstChild`, `GetAttribute`, and table lookups can return nil at any time
Writing `if x = nil then` — use `==` for comparison

examples.title: nil in everyday Roblox code
examples.code:
local part = workspace:FindFirstChild("MissingPart")
print(part)                 --> nil (not found)

if part == nil then
    warn("Part does not exist!")
end

-- Roblox's nil guard, classic pattern:
local spawn = workspace:FindFirstChild("SpawnLocation")
if spawn then
    print("Spawn is at", spawn.Position)
end
examples.commonMistake: Using the result of FindFirstChild directly (`workspace:FindFirstChild("X").Position`) crashes when the object doesn't exist. Always guard first.

examples.title: nil removes table entries
examples.code:
local inventory = { sword = true, potion = true }
inventory.sword = nil       -- delete the key
print(inventory.sword)      --> nil
print(inventory.potion)     --> true
